flags.summary: May 31, 2023: Crashed his pickup through a guardrail at I-65 and Indiana 11 and drove away; a trooper's affidavit reported a 0.097% portable breath test more than an hour later. On June 12, 2023 he pleaded guilty to misdemeanor operating while intoxicated and leaving the scene, receiving suspended sentences, probation and about $4,000 in restitution; he kept his seat. He said he took "full responsibility," apologized and was "already enrolled in counseling". In December 2023 a judge ended his probation after six months, finding he had completed its conditions.
flags.note: Misdemeanor OWI and leaving-the-scene plea, 2023; probation ended early. Previously shown in the public profile.

flags.summary: Jan. 30, 2024: Briefly opened his jacket to show a holstered handgun while talking with Muncie students at a gun-safety rally. Speaker Todd Huston said he should not have done so; Democratic leaders criticized it. Lucas said "There was no intimidation whatsoever" and that the episode was "being intentionally blown out of proportion".
flags.note: Showing a holstered handgun to students at a gun-safety rally; relates to his gun-policy work. Previously shown in the public profile.

flags.summary: August 2022: Was criticized, including by the CANDLES Holocaust Museum, for a Facebook cover photo with a quote attributed to Joseph Goebbels; he deleted it and replaced it with a different quote. The report noted earlier criticism of his social-media posts and that Speaker Huston had previously removed him from study committees over a meme.
flags.note: Removed from the profile as non-policy. Other 2017-2022 social-media controversies were not read in full.
